proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but the Agreement contains no operative indemnity at all, so we have no protection against third-party IP infringement claims arising from the Works or from Contractor's misconduct. We have added a Contractor indemnity in line with our playbook position (IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Company data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics; if helpful we can discuss customary exclusions (Company modifications, combinations and specifications) and a super-cap in place of the uncapped carve-out.

ops.text: (d) INDEMNIFICATION BY CONTRACTOR. Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services, Works or any Contractor Information infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim, Contractor shall have sole control of the defense and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent), and Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Notwithstanding Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c), Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to any limitation or exclusion of liability or waiver of attorneys' fees set out in this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Insert a Contractor (Vendor) indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Company data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard claim procedure and a carve-out from the liability cap and fee waiver.

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains no operative indemnity language of any kind — only a liability cap (p0035), a consequential-damages exclusion (p0036) and an attorneys' fees waiver (p0037). A full-text search for "indemn" returns only the heading, and Section 5 provides a non-infringement warranty (p0026) but no defence or indemnity obligation; the cap's carve-out for "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9" points to the Independent Contractor clause, confirming the indemnity was never included. With no Vendor IP indemnity at all, the Agreement falls into walk-away territory and fails both the preferred and fallback positions. We inserted a Contractor indemnity as new Section 7(d) covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Company data and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a carve-out from the Section 7 limitations so the indemnity is not neutralised. No Customer indemnity exists, so no narrowing is required; the liability cap itself is addressed under LOL-CAP rather than double-flagged here.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
rationale: Section 4 achieves substantially the preferred position and is not redlined. Works (including deliverables, inventions, programs, documentation and data prepared for us under a SOW) vest in Clear Capital, with Contractor obliged to execute further documents and, on termination, expressly assigning all right, title and interest in Works in progress (p0033, p0044). Contractor retains only its own pre-existing tools, methodologies and know-how (p0020) — which the playbook expressly accepts — and grants us a royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivatives of any Contractor's Information embedded in the Works for our business operations (p0021). There is no assignment or licence of Clear Capital IP or data to Contractor, and no joint ownership; our data supplied in the course of the Services is protected as Confidential Information (p0038). Minor sub-elements short of preferred, noted but not flagged: ownership vests as invoices are paid rather than on creation (consistent with the rule's "we own what we pay for" premise, and backstopped by the assignment of Works in progress on final payment); the licence-back is not styled "irrevocable" or "worldwide"; and there is no express standalone sentence confirming we retain all rights in Customer Data. These would be worth picking up in a future amendment or SOW but do not fail the fallback.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 for both parties and carved out confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, since indemnities and confidentiality breaches must sit outside the cap. We have also confirmed that our obligation to pay fees due is not itself capped; we can discuss a straight 12-month fee cap if the fixed floor is an issue.

ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS AND CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, EACH PARTY'S MAXIMUM AGGREGATE LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF (I) THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID OR PAYABLE TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (USD 1,000,000). COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES AND EXPENSES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

ops.text: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, NONE OF WHICH SHALL BE SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 for both parties, exclude Company's payment obligations, and add standard uncapped carve-outs.

quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, and 7(b) waives consequential damages mutually, so the mutuality element is satisfied. However, the cap fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the only carve-out is "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", and Paragraph 9 is the Independent Contractor/tax provision (there is no indemnification clause anywhere in the document despite the Section 7 caption) — so there are no carve-outs for confidentiality (Section 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, indemnification or infringement of Company IP, even though Contractor gives an unqualified non-infringement warranty at Section 5(c). Second, Contractor's cap is measured per Statement of Work by reference only to fees actually paid for those particular Services, which on a time-and-materials engagement can fall well below 12 months' fees, and there is no USD floor. The redline sets a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, preserves the existing Paragraph 9 carve-out, confirms our fee payment obligation is not "damages" for cap purposes, and adds one Excluded Claims sentence placing confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out so we may assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and so RadialSpark cannot assign to one of our competitors; our playbook does not permit corporate reorganizations or M&A to be gated on vendor consent. If helpful, we can instead make the successor right mutual on written notice.

ops.newText: which will not be unreasonably withheld; provided, however, that Company may assign this Agreement, without Contractor's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business, and Contractor shall not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Company.
ops.oldText: which will not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add Company affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and bar assignment by Contractor to a Company competitor

quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 10 is symmetrical and applies a "not unreasonably withheld" consent standard, but it contains no carve-out permitting Clear Capital to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. The fallback position requires at least a right to assign to successors (with notice), so consent-gated M&A/reorganization assignment fails the fallback on a material term. There is no competitor restriction on RadialSpark's assignment either. Termination (Section 6, p0031–p0033) contains no change-of-control trigger and the document has no change-of-control language anywhere, so there is no vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control — that aspect is fine. Minimal redline inserts the affiliate/successor carve-out for Company and bars assignment by Contractor to a Company competitor, reaching the preferred position without disturbing the mutual consent standard or the subcontracting restriction.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Clear Capital, meeting the preferred position (not merely the fallback). Section 1(a) retains Contractor only "on a task by task basis," with scope and volume committed solely through individually negotiated Statements of Work, so we remain free to procure comparable consulting services from other suppliers; Section 2 (p0011) adds no minimum-commitment or exclusive-dealing term. Targeted searches for "exclusive," "sole/exclusive provider," "exclusively," requirements-contract language, and "shall not procure/retain/engage" surfaced no customer-side restrictive covenant. The three "exclusive" hits are unrelated and none restrict our sourcing: p0020 concerns Contractor's retained ownership of pre-existing property, p0021 grants us a royalty-free non-exclusive license (a benefit to us), and p0051 is a standard entire-agreement clause. The apparent numbering gap at Section 2 flagged in the planner hints is resolved: the TERM provision is present as p0011 within the Section 1 paragraph run, so no exclusivity text is missing from the reviewed text. No redline proposed.

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, forfeiture, minimum-fee or early-termination fee payable by Clear Capital. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "stipulated", "minimum" and "forfeit" return nothing, and the compensation section (§ 3) imposes only time-and-materials fees, expenses and taxes with no late-payment penalty or interest. Termination under § 6(a) (convenience on 15 days' notice with no uncompleted SOW) and § 6(b)/7(c) requires only payment of fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the termination date, which is ordinary accrued-consideration language rather than a stipulated damages amount. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: Section 4 is primarily an assignment of Works to Clear Capital (p0017), with a residual licence-back for RadialSpark's retained pre-existing materials in § 4(c). That grant meets the rule's material terms: it is royalty-free, non-exclusive and expressly perpetual, with no revocation right anywhere in the Agreement (no "revocable" or "non-transferable" language appears), so RadialSpark cannot pull the licence at will. Affiliates and contractors are not named, but the express right to grant sublicences gives us a clear path to extend use to affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, which is at least as good as the fallback's "affiliates covered on written notice"; § 4(d) further confirms we may engage others to modify the delivered software. The licence scope ("in connection with Company's business operations") is broad rather than limited to internal use. Minor shortfalls short of the preferred position, noted but not flagged: there is no express successor-transfer right for the licence, so transfer runs through the general nonassignability clause (p0042), which requires the other party's consent "which will not be unreasonably withheld" — a workable M&A path — and affiliates/contractors are covered indirectly by sublicensing rather than being named.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
rationale: This is a presence rule and the agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding Clear Capital, so it meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). Searches for "compet", "exclusiv", "solicit", "shall not", "may not"/"agrees not to" and field-of-use phrasings surfaced nothing restricting the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The only restrictive covenant is the mutual, one-year employee non-solicit in § 13 (p0047), which is a separate term and applies equally to both parties. The sole "Company shall not" language (p0020) is a scope-of-use limit on the Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials — an IP licence-scope matter, not a restraint on our business, and § 4(c) (p0021) grants us a perpetual licence to use that material in our business operations. Section 4(b) (p0019) runs in the opposite direction, preserving the Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which is a restriction-free position for the vendor and not something we would flag. No redline required.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Company right to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on 30 days' notice, because Section 6(a) permits convenience termination only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, leaving us locked into in-flight engagements under an indefinite term. Our playbook requires a customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with no early-termination penalty and a refund of prepaid fees; we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: (c) In addition, Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part and for any or no reason, upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, without penalty, early-termination charge or forfeiture of any amounts. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses incurred or earned for Services properly performed through the effective date of such termination, Contractor shall refund to Company any prepaid fees for the period after such effective date, and Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

proposal.summary: Add Company termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice covering outstanding Statements of Work, with no penalty and refund of prepaid fees.

quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
rationale: Section 6 gives a convenience right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," so while any Statement of Work is in flight neither party — including us — may terminate without cause; the only other exit (6(b)) requires an uncured material breach. Because the term is evergreen (Section 2: continues until terminated under Paragraph 6) and Statements of Work are the operative vehicle for all Services, we effectively have no convenience right for engagements running well beyond 12 months. That fails both the preferred position (Customer convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice), and sits in walk-away territory. We therefore propose a new Section 6(c) giving Company a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement and any Statement of Work, with Contractor paid only for Services performed, prepaid fees refunded, and work in progress assigned. The Contractor-side 15-day convenience right in 6(a) is tolerable as drafted because it can only be exercised when no Statement of Work is outstanding (i.e., no active engagement to abandon), so we have not disturbed it.

quote: (b) Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "records" and "premises" return no audit, inspection or verification right exercisable against Clear Capital. The compensation section (§ 3) is one-directional: Contractor invoices with supporting detail and Company pays; it grants RadialSpark no right to examine our books, usage or systems, and no other section (§§ 1, 4–7) creates one. Because the agreement imposes no audit obligation on us, there is nothing to limit as to frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, and the position sits at or above the preferred standard by default. Noted only for the record: since no audit right exists, we also have no negotiated cost-shifting threshold — no change needed, as the absence operates entirely in our favour. If RadialSpark later proposes a compensation-verification or usage-audit right, it should be capped at once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, conducted off-site by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at RadialSpark's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, with no direct access to our systems.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Arizona to New York and added exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our playbook's accepted jurisdictions. If New York does not work for you, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London.

ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof. The parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

proposal.summary: Replace Arizona governing law with New York law and add exclusive venue in New York County courts

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
rationale: Section 11 (Severability; Governing Law) selects Arizona law, which is outside the playbook's accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales, so the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback positions on a material term. Arizona is also effectively the Contractor-favorable choice here, with no offsetting benefit to us. Separately, the Agreement contains no forum, venue, or jurisdiction provision anywhere (searches for jurisdiction, venue, arbitration and courts returned nothing, and the preamble contains only entity recitals), leaving the dispute forum entirely unspecified; there is at least no mandatory arbitration seated abroad, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away territory. Consistent with the redline guidance to change only the jurisdiction words and forum, the proposed edit swaps "Arizona" for "the State of New York" and appends an exclusive-jurisdiction sentence for the state and federal courts in New York County, reaching the preferred position while leaving the severability language and the conflict-of-laws carve-out intact. The comment offers Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London as the fallback if New York is resisted.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale:
The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation of any kind, and none burdening us. Pricing is set exclusively per-Statement of Work on a time-and-materials basis (§ 3(a), p0013), with invoicing mechanics in § 3(b) (p0014); neither creates any parity, price-matching, or best-terms commitment. Targeted searches for "no less favorable", "most favored", and regex patterns covering favourable/favorable, most-favoured-nation, best price/pricing, matching third-party offers, other customers, exclusivity, preferred provider and comparable terms returned no MFN language anywhere in the document, and full reads of § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) and § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) — the sections where such a term would sit — confirm its absence. Confirmed from the preamble (p0002) that "Company" is Clear Capital (our party) and "Contractor" is RadialSpark, so there is no risk of a mis-directed reading.

This is the preferred position: no MFN obligation on Customer. Note this is not a "missing" finding — the rule expects the absence of such a clause, so absence is full compliance rather than a gap to fill; we would only flag if we were required to extend RadialSpark our best third-party terms. Separately noted but not flagged here: § 3(b) permits the Contractor to "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" without a cap. That is an uncapped price-uplift concern belonging to the pricing/price-increase rule, not an MFN parity obligation, and flagging it under this rule would double-count the same commercial term. No redline proposed.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on Clear Capital, so it meets the preferred position rather than merely the fallback. Compensation under § 3(a) is time-and-materials as set out in each Statement of Work, and § 1(a) engages Contractor only "on a task by task basis," meaning Clear Capital pays solely for services it actually orders. There is no committed spend to reduce or true up, and § 6(a) additionally permits either party to terminate for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding, so no multi-year lock-in exists. A full-text search for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "retainer", "take or pay" and "volume" returned only unrelated hits (exclusive property/licence in § 4 and the entire-agreement clause in § 7). Noted for context only, and not a deviation under this rule: § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice, which is a pricing rather than a commitment issue and belongs to any price-increase rule. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches so that neither party breaches this section merely by running an untargeted job posting or hiring someone who approaches it on their own initiative. The rest of the clause (mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, no no-hire) is acceptable to us as drafted.

ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Section shall restrict either party from (a) making general solicitations for employment or engagement that are not specifically directed at the other party's personnel (including advertisements, job postings and searches by recruiting firms not targeted at such personnel), or (b) employing or engaging any person who responds to such a general solicitation or who approaches such party on an unsolicited basis.
ops.oldText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicit.

quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital with a non-solicit. It already meets most of the fallback: it is mutual, runs only 12 months (well inside the 24-month walk-away line), is limited to personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, and is a solicitation restriction rather than a prohibited no-hire. It fails the fallback on one material term, however: there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches, which the rule summary treats as a condition of acceptability ("only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out"). As drafted, an untargeted job posting answered by a RadialSpark engineer could put us in breach. We therefore propose the minimal fallback edit — a single carve-out sentence for untargeted solicitations and unsolicited approaches — rather than the preferred position (no non-solicit at all), which would be disproportionate given the clause is mutual and otherwise narrow. Separately noted but not flagged: the 12 months runs from termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement, a minor variance from the preferred formulation.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
rationale: There is no auto-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (no "renew" language, no renewal term, and no price-uplift or rate-increase provisions). Instead, § 2 creates an evergreen term that continues until terminated under § 6, and § 6(a) lets either party — including us — terminate for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding. That structure is at least as favourable to us as the preferred position (no automatic renewal, exit on well under 30 days' notice, no committed multi-year renewal, no unilateral price escalation), so there is nothing to redline. Noted only for completeness: because there is no renewal pricing mechanic, fee changes would need to be agreed in each Statement of Work; if we later add renewal terms we should carry in the CPI/3% uplift cap.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard exit provision: on termination we can purchase up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, and our data, Works and Confidential Information are returned within 30 days in a machine-readable format and then deleted with written certification. The Agreement is currently silent on data return and wind-down, which leaves us without access to our own records; we can accept 90 days of transition assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: (c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days, return to Company all Company data, Works and Confidential Information in Contractor's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data, Works and Confidential Information from its systems and certify such deletion to Company in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation in Section 6

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
rationale: Section 6 (and the duplicate termination text at p0044) addresses only final payment and assignment of Works in progress; it says nothing about transition assistance, return of Company data or deletion/certification. Section 4 covers ownership of Works but not delivery back of our data, and the confidentiality provision (p0038-p0040) imposes only use/disclosure restrictions with no return-or-destroy obligation. No usable clause exists anywhere in the Agreement, so the rule is missing. We inserted the preferred position at Section 6(c): up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of Company data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and deletion with written certification thereafter; 90 days of assistance with a 30-day export would be an acceptable fallback.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5 contains no warranty that the Services and Works will conform to the Specifications, and no remedy if they do not, so we have added a 90-day conformity warranty with re-performance, repair or refund. This matches our standard position that the Contractor stands behind its work for a defined period.

ops.text: (e) Contractor represents and warrants to Company that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, and (ii) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each of the Works and any deliverables will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and documentation. Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Contractor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Services or Works, or a refund of the fees paid for such non-conforming Services or Works.

proposal.summary: Add express conformity-to-Specifications warranty (90 days) with repair/re-perform/refund remedy

quote: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
rationale: Section 5's express warranties cover only legal compliance, authority/rights, non-infringement and anti-bribery. There is no warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications or documentation, no warranty duration, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; Section 1(b) contains only a general workmanlike performance covenant, and Section 4, despite its "ACCEPTANCE" heading, contains no acceptance or rejection mechanic that could serve as a practical remedy. The clause therefore fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). The disclaimer in 5(e) preserves express warranties, so no carve-out is needed; we added a 90-day conformity warranty with a re-performance, repair or refund remedy and renumbered the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The insurance covenant covers workers' compensation, general liability and E&O but omits cyber/privacy coverage, and Contractor accesses our systems and handles our data and Confidential Information. quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Contrary to the planner's assumption, an insurance covenant does exist at § 7 ¶ 14 (p0048). It carries workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000, and certificates/evidence of insurance on Company request with notice of material change — so the general liability, workers' comp and certificate elements are satisfied, and E&O sits at the playbook fallback level (USD 1M rather than the preferred USD 2M), which we note but do not redline. The material gap is cyber/privacy liability, which the fallback requires at USD 2,000,000. Contractor plainly touches our data: Confidential Information is defined at p0038 as documents, software, reports, data and records obtained by Contractor from Company in performing Services, and p0007 contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. With no cyber coverage at all for a vendor that handles our data and systems, the clause fails the fallback on that term. Minimal fix: insert cyber liability (network security and privacy) coverage of USD 5,000,000, scoped to where Contractor processes Company data, leaving the remaining coverages and the existing certificate mechanic untouched; USD 2,000,000 is offered as the fallback in the comment.
